topics: Introduction to the Nursing Process in Midwifery

questions.question_text: Which statement best defines the nursing process in midwifery?

choices.text: A routine checklist used only during antenatal visits
A systematic, patient-centred approach to identifying and meeting the health needs of mothers and babies
A medical procedure performed exclusively by obstetricians
A method of recording hospital admissions and discharges

questions.rationale: The nursing process is a systematic and logical framework for providing individualized nursing care. In midwifery, it guides care for women, newborns and families across pregnancy, labour and the postnatal period.

questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly represents the five phases of the traditional nursing process?

choices.text: Assessment, planning, diagnosis, evaluation, implementation
Diagnosis, assessment, implementation, planning, evaluation
Assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation, evaluation
Planning, assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, implementation

questions.rationale: The traditional nursing process follows the sequence assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation. Each phase builds on information and decisions made during the preceding phases.

questions.question_text: Which characteristic makes the nursing process appropriate for family-centred midwifery care?

choices.text: It allows the midwife to make every decision without consultation
It focuses only on the mother's physical condition
It encourages individualized care and participation of the woman and her family where appropriate
It requires every woman to receive an identical care plan

questions.rationale: Family-centred care recognizes the woman as an active participant in decisions about her health and her baby's wellbeing. The midwife should consider her preferences, needs, cultural context and appropriate family support.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the assessment phase of the nursing process?

choices.text: To collect and validate information about the woman's health status
To determine whether all planned interventions have succeeded
To select nursing interventions before identifying health needs
To discharge the woman from the maternity unit

questions.rationale: Assessment involves systematic collection, validation, organization and documentation of relevant health information. Accurate assessment provides the evidence needed for nursing diagnoses and care planning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of subjective data collected during antenatal assessment?

choices.text: Blood pressure of 110/70 mmHg
The woman's report of persistent headache
Haemoglobin concentration of 10 g/dL
Observed bilateral ankle oedema

questions.rationale: Subjective data are symptoms or experiences reported by the woman and cannot usually be directly measured by the midwife. A headache described by the woman is subjective, whereas blood pressure and observed oedema are objective findings.

questions.question_text: Which method is most appropriate for obtaining a woman's obstetric history during her first antenatal visit?

choices.text: Observing her walking into the clinic
Reviewing only her blood pressure reading
Conducting a structured interview using relevant open and closed questions
Asking another patient to describe her previous pregnancies

questions.rationale: A structured interview enables the midwife to obtain relevant information about previous pregnancies, births, medical conditions and current concerns. Open questions encourage the woman to explain her experiences, while focused questions clarify important details.

questions.question_text: What is a nursing diagnosis?

choices.text: A medical identification of the disease causing a patient's symptoms
A clinical judgement about a person's response to actual or potential health conditions
A prescription for medication issued by a midwife
A laboratory report confirming a medical condition

questions.rationale: A nursing diagnosis describes a human response to health conditions or life processes that nursing care can address. It differs from a medical diagnosis, which identifies a disease or pathological condition.

questions.question_text: Which component is essential in a correctly formulated problem-focused nursing diagnosis using the PES format?

choices.text: Patient name, examination and treatment
Problem, aetiology and signs or symptoms
Procedure, evaluation and supervision
Prognosis, emergency and solution

questions.rationale: The PES format represents the problem, related aetiology and defining signs or symptoms. It helps the midwife communicate the identified nursing problem and the evidence supporting it.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes a measurable expected outcome in a midwifery care plan?

choices.text: The woman will feel better soon
The midwife will provide good care throughout admission
The woman will report reduced pain from 8/10 to 3/10 within one hour after appropriate interventions
The woman will be comfortable whenever possible

questions.rationale: An expected outcome should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound. A measurable pain score and defined time frame allow the midwife to evaluate whether the intervention has achieved its intended effect.

questions.question_text: Which activity is an example of an indirect nursing intervention?

choices.text: Assisting a woman to change position during labour
Providing breastfeeding education to a mother
Coordinating a referral for a woman with suspected severe pre-eclampsia
Measuring a newborn's temperature

questions.rationale: Indirect nursing interventions support patient care without involving direct physical contact with the patient at the time of the activity. Coordination of referrals and communication with other healthcare professionals are examples.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of the evaluation phase of the nursing process?

choices.text: To determine whether the expected patient outcomes have been achieved
To collect the woman's initial health history
To identify a medical diagnosis without further assessment
To prepare a list of medications before admission

questions.rationale: Evaluation compares the woman's current condition with the expected outcomes established during planning. The findings guide decisions to continue, modify or discontinue nursing interventions.

questions.question_text: In the SOAP method of documentation, what does the letter A represent?

choices.text: Admission
Assessment
Action
Administration

questions.rationale: SOAP stands for Subjective, Objective, Assessment and Plan. The assessment section records the healthcare professional's clinical interpretation of the subjective and objective findings.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a partograph or labour care monitoring tool during labour?

choices.text: To document only the medications administered during labour
To monitor maternal and fetal wellbeing and the progress of labour
To determine the baby's sex before delivery
To replace the need for clinical assessment

questions.rationale: Labour monitoring tools support systematic observation of labour progress and maternal and fetal wellbeing. They help identify abnormalities early and prompt appropriate clinical action.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes critical thinking in midwifery practice?

choices.text: Following instructions without considering the woman's condition
Making clinical decisions based only on personal experience
Using evidence, clinical knowledge and logical judgement to make appropriate care decisions
Avoiding consultation when a clinical situation is uncertain

questions.rationale: Critical thinking involves objective analysis, interpretation and evaluation of relevant information. It enables midwives to make reasoned decisions and recognize when further assessment or referral is necessary.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of objective data obtained during a postnatal assessment?

choices.text: The mother reports feeling dizzy
The mother states that breastfeeding is painful
The midwife observes a boggy uterus on abdominal palpation
The mother says she is worried about her newborn

questions.rationale: Objective data are findings observed, measured or verified by the healthcare professional. A boggy uterus identified during examination is an objective finding that may indicate inadequate uterine contraction.

questions.question_text: Which principle should guide the selection of nursing interventions in an individualized midwifery care plan?

choices.text: Interventions should be based on identified needs, evidence and the woman's preferences
Every woman should receive the same interventions regardless of assessment findings
Interventions should be selected only according to the midwife's convenience
The woman's preferences should always be excluded from clinical decisions

questions.rationale: Nursing interventions should address identified health needs and be supported by current evidence and professional standards. The woman should be involved in decisions wherever possible, while urgent clinical risks must be managed appropriately.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes direct nursing care from indirect nursing care?

choices.text: Direct care involves patient contact, while indirect care supports the patient through activities such as coordination and documentation
Direct care is performed only by doctors, while indirect care is performed only by midwives
Direct care involves documentation, while indirect care involves all physical examinations
There is no difference between direct and indirect nursing care

questions.rationale: Direct care involves activities performed with or for the woman or newborn, such as examination, education and physical assistance. Indirect care includes activities such as care coordination, documentation and arranging referrals.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman attends a CHPS compound for her first antenatal visit. She reports a previous stillbirth, but the available antenatal record contains no details of that pregnancy. What should the midwife do next?

choices.text: Ignore the information because it is not recorded in the antenatal card
Record the woman's account, ask relevant follow-up questions and seek available supporting records
Immediately diagnose recurrent stillbirth
Delay all antenatal assessment until the previous hospital sends a report

questions.rationale: The midwife should obtain a detailed obstetric history and document the information provided by the woman. Available records may help validate the history, but their absence should not prevent appropriate current assessment and risk evaluation.

questions.question_text: During antenatal assessment, a woman at 32 weeks of gestation reports a severe headache and blurred vision. Her blood pressure is 166/112 mmHg. What should the midwife do FIRST?

choices.text: Advise her to rest at home and return the following week
Arrange routine urine testing before taking further action
Recognize suspected severe pre-eclampsia and initiate urgent assessment, stabilization and referral according to protocol
Provide reassurance because headache is common in pregnancy

questions.rationale: Severe hypertension with headache and visual disturbance suggests pre-eclampsia with severe features and carries a risk of maternal and fetal complications. Immediate clinical assessment, appropriate stabilization and urgent escalation are required rather than routine follow-up.

questions.question_text: A midwife is interviewing a pregnant woman who speaks a local language that the midwife does not understand. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Proceed using gestures without checking whether the woman understands
Use an appropriate trained interpreter and maintain the woman's privacy
Ask another patient in the waiting area to interpret sensitive information
Omit the interview and document that the woman refused to provide information

questions.rationale: Effective communication is necessary for accurate assessment and informed participation in care. A suitable interpreter should be used while protecting confidentiality and allowing the woman to express her concerns freely.

questions.question_text: A woman at 28 weeks of gestation attends an antenatal clinic and reports that she has not felt fetal movements since the previous evening. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Reassure her that reduced fetal movement is normal in the third trimester
Advise her to wait until the next antenatal appointment
Arrange prompt clinical assessment of fetal wellbeing according to the facility's protocol
Prescribe iron tablets without further assessment

questions.rationale: A significant reduction or absence of fetal movement requires prompt assessment because it may indicate fetal compromise. The midwife should not dismiss the complaint or delay assessment until the next routine visit.

questions.question_text: During an antenatal physical examination, which action should the midwife take before performing abdominal palpation?

choices.text: Explain the procedure, obtain consent and ensure privacy
Ask the woman to remove all her clothing without explanation
Begin palpation immediately to save time
Ask the woman's companion to perform the examination

questions.rationale: The midwife should explain the examination, obtain informed consent and maintain the woman's dignity and privacy. These actions support respectful maternity care and promote cooperation during assessment.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman attending a CHPS compound has a temperature of 39°C, chills and general body weakness. What should the midwife do FIRST?

choices.text: Document the temperature and allow her to return home
Assess her condition promptly, identify danger signs and arrange appropriate investigations and treatment or referral
Assume she has malaria and provide treatment without assessment
Advise her to drink water and return after one week

questions.rationale: Fever in pregnancy may result from malaria or other infections and can become serious for both mother and fetus. The midwife should assess severity, investigate according to protocol and initiate appropriate treatment or referral.

questions.question_text: A woman in labour reports severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. Her blood pressure is falling and she appears pale and restless. Which nursing problem should receive priority attention?

choices.text: Disturbed sleep pattern
Risk for impaired skin integrity
Deficient fluid volume associated with suspected obstetric haemorrhage
Readiness for enhanced knowledge about breastfeeding

questions.rationale: The woman's pallor, bleeding and falling blood pressure suggest significant blood loss and possible haemodynamic instability. Circulatory compromise is an immediate threat to life and takes priority over non-urgent problems.

questions.question_text: A midwife identifies acute pain related to uterine contractions in a woman in labour. Which finding would best support this nursing diagnosis?

choices.text: The woman reports pain rated 8/10 during contractions
The woman's blood group is O positive
The woman has a history of childhood immunization
The woman's antenatal booking date is recorded

questions.rationale: A woman's report of pain intensity is relevant subjective evidence supporting an acute pain diagnosis. The midwife should also assess the location, pattern, duration and associated findings to guide appropriate care.

questions.question_text: Four women are being cared for in a maternity unit. Which woman should the midwife assess FIRST?

choices.text: A woman requesting assistance with breastfeeding positioning
A woman with severe vaginal bleeding and signs of shock
A woman reporting mild lower back discomfort during pregnancy
A woman requesting information about her discharge date

questions.rationale: Severe vaginal bleeding with signs of shock indicates a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate intervention. Using the principle of prioritizing physiological threats, the midwife should attend to this woman before the other patients.

questions.question_text: A woman in labour is anxious because she does not understand what is happening. Her vital signs are stable, fetal heart rate is reassuring and labour is progressing normally. Which nursing diagnosis is most appropriate?

choices.text: Impaired gas exchange
Deficient fluid volume
Anxiety related to uncertainty about the labour process
Ineffective airway clearance

questions.rationale: The woman's expressed fear and uncertainty support an anxiety diagnosis. Therapeutic communication, reassurance and clear explanations can help reduce anxiety while continuing routine maternal and fetal monitoring.

questions.question_text: A postpartum woman has a boggy uterus, heavy vaginal bleeding and a pulse rate of 124 beats per minute. Which action should the midwife take FIRST?

choices.text: Provide routine breastfeeding education
Initiate the postpartum haemorrhage response, including immediate uterine massage and calling for emergency assistance
Complete the discharge summary
Encourage the woman to walk around the ward

questions.rationale: A boggy uterus with heavy bleeding and tachycardia suggests postpartum haemorrhage, commonly associated with uterine atony. Immediate action, emergency assistance and management according to the facility's haemorrhage protocol are essential.

questions.question_text: A midwife is applying Maslow's hierarchy of needs when prioritizing care for a postpartum woman. Which need should generally receive priority when it is immediately threatened?

choices.text: The woman's desire for social interaction
The woman's need for recognition and achievement
The woman's physiological need for adequate breathing and circulation
The woman's desire for personal development

questions.rationale: Maslow's hierarchy places physiological needs, including breathing and circulation, at the foundational level. Immediate threats to these functions generally take priority over social, esteem and self-actualization needs.

questions.question_text: A woman in labour has a nursing diagnosis of acute pain related to uterine contractions. Which expected outcome is most appropriate?

choices.text: The woman will never experience pain during labour
The woman will demonstrate improved coping and report acceptable pain relief within the agreed period
The midwife will complete all routine documentation
The woman will deliver within thirty minutes

questions.rationale: An appropriate outcome should be realistic, measurable and relevant to the identified problem. Improved coping and an acceptable level of pain relief can be assessed without making unrealistic promises about eliminating labour pain.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman has been diagnosed with iron-deficiency anaemia. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate to include in her care plan?

choices.text: Advise her to stop eating iron-rich foods
Provide education on iron-rich foods, adherence to prescribed iron supplementation and follow-up assessment
Recommend that she discontinue all antenatal visits
Advise her to take iron tablets only when she feels tired

questions.rationale: Management of iron-deficiency anaemia includes appropriate supplementation, dietary education and monitoring of response to treatment. The midwife should reinforce adherence and arrange follow-up according to the woman's clinical condition and local protocol.

questions.question_text: A midwife is planning care for a woman with gestational diabetes. Which outcome is most appropriate?

choices.text: The woman will understand the agreed dietary and activity plan and demonstrate appropriate blood glucose monitoring
The woman will avoid all carbohydrate-containing foods
The woman will stop attending antenatal clinic when glucose improves
The woman will deliver immediately after diagnosis

questions.rationale: Care planning for gestational diabetes should promote appropriate glycaemic control through individualized nutrition, physical activity where suitable and monitoring. Ongoing antenatal review is necessary to assess maternal and fetal wellbeing.

questions.question_text: A woman at 36 weeks of gestation is at risk of developing complications because of hypertension. Which intervention should be included in her care plan?

choices.text: Advise her to avoid all physical movement and remain at home without review
Monitor blood pressure and assess for symptoms of severe disease, with timely escalation when indicated
Discontinue all prescribed medication without consultation
Delay assessment until after delivery

questions.rationale: Hypertension in pregnancy requires ongoing maternal assessment and appropriate fetal surveillance according to clinical findings and protocol. Monitoring for severe features allows timely treatment, referral or delivery planning when necessary.

questions.question_text: A primiparous mother wishes to breastfeed but is unsure how to position her newborn. Which planned intervention best supports her expected outcome?

choices.text: Discourage her from breastfeeding until the newborn is one month old
Provide practical assistance with positioning and attachment, then assess the baby's latch
Recommend routine water supplementation after every feed
Ask her to learn breastfeeding techniques without assistance

questions.rationale: Practical breastfeeding support helps the mother establish effective positioning and attachment. Observing a feed enables the midwife to identify difficulties and provide individualized guidance.

questions.question_text: A midwife is developing a postnatal care plan for a mother and newborn. Which approach best reflects family-centred care?

choices.text: Exclude the mother from decisions because the midwife has professional training
Involve the mother in decisions, address her concerns and support appropriate family participation with her consent
Allow family members to make all decisions without consulting the mother
Provide information only when the mother requests discharge

questions.rationale: Family-centred care respects the mother's autonomy and recognizes the importance of supportive family involvement. The midwife should communicate clearly and obtain the mother's consent before involving relatives in personal health discussions.

questions.question_text: A woman in the first stage of labour is stable and requests assistance with coping with contractions. Which intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Encourage appropriate breathing and relaxation techniques and provide continuous emotional support
Leave the woman alone until the second stage of labour
Restrict all communication with the woman
Perform an unnecessary vaginal examination during every contraction

questions.rationale: Supportive care, breathing techniques and relaxation can help a woman cope with labour. The midwife should continue appropriate maternal and fetal monitoring and avoid unnecessary interventions.

questions.question_text: During the immediate postnatal period, a stable mother delivers a healthy term newborn. Which action best supports early newborn care?

choices.text: Separate the newborn from the mother routinely for observation
Dry the newborn, assess breathing, maintain warmth and support immediate skin-to-skin contact when appropriate
Bathe the newborn immediately before initiating breastfeeding
Give water before the first breastfeed

questions.rationale: Immediate newborn care includes drying, assessment of breathing, thermal protection and early skin-to-skin contact when mother and baby are stable. These measures support newborn adaptation and early initiation of breastfeeding.

questions.question_text: A woman in labour develops an abnormal fetal heart rate pattern suggesting possible fetal compromise. What should the midwife do FIRST?

choices.text: Continue routine monitoring without reassessment
Promptly assess the situation, initiate appropriate immediate measures and escalate for urgent obstetric review
Wait until the next scheduled antenatal appointment
Record the finding only after delivery

questions.rationale: An abnormal fetal heart rate may indicate fetal compromise and requires prompt clinical assessment. The midwife should initiate appropriate measures, summon assistance and arrange timely intervention according to the clinical situation and facility protocol.

questions.question_text: A woman who has just delivered is found to have a boggy uterus during routine postnatal assessment. Which immediate nursing action is appropriate?

choices.text: Assess uterine tone and initiate uterine massage while evaluating bleeding and obtaining assistance as indicated
Encourage the woman to sleep and reassess the following morning
Discharge the woman immediately
Withhold all assessment until the placenta is examined

questions.rationale: A boggy uterus may indicate uterine atony, a major cause of postpartum haemorrhage. The midwife should act promptly, assess blood loss and the woman's condition, and follow the facility's postpartum haemorrhage protocol.

questions.question_text: A mother at a postnatal clinic reports that her newborn has difficulty feeding and is unusually sleepy. What should the midwife do?

choices.text: Advise her to wait until the next immunization appointment
Assess the newborn promptly for danger signs and arrange urgent referral if serious illness is suspected
Recommend giving herbal preparations before breastfeeding
Reassure her that all newborns are sleepy and feeding difficulties are normal

questions.rationale: Poor feeding and unusual lethargy may be signs of serious neonatal illness, including infection or other complications. Prompt assessment and referral are necessary rather than delaying care or recommending unverified remedies.

questions.question_text: A midwife at a CHPS compound identifies a pregnant woman with suspected severe pre-eclampsia. The facility cannot provide definitive emergency obstetric care. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Keep the woman at the CHPS compound until the next routine clinic day
Initiate appropriate emergency measures within the midwife's competence and arrange urgent referral to a facility capable of definitive management
Advise the woman to seek treatment from a traditional healer
Send the woman home to collect her antenatal card before making any referral arrangements

questions.rationale: Suspected severe pre-eclampsia requires urgent assessment and access to appropriate emergency obstetric care. The midwife should initiate indicated stabilization measures, communicate with the receiving facility and arrange safe referral without unnecessary delay.

questions.question_text: A woman received nursing interventions for pain during labour. Which finding best indicates that the planned outcome has been achieved?

choices.text: The midwife has completed the care plan form
The woman reports improved coping and a reduction in pain to her agreed acceptable level
The woman has remained in the same position throughout labour
The woman's relative reports that the midwife was helpful

questions.rationale: Evaluation should be based on evidence that relates directly to the expected outcome. The woman's reported pain level and ability to cope provide relevant information about the effectiveness of the interventions.

questions.question_text: A postpartum woman was receiving care for ineffective breastfeeding. After assistance with positioning, the newborn still has difficulty attaching to the breast. What should the midwife do next?

choices.text: Discontinue breastfeeding support because the first intervention failed
Reassess the mother and newborn, identify contributing factors and modify the care plan
Document that the outcome has been achieved
Blame the mother for not following instructions

questions.rationale: Failure to achieve the expected outcome indicates the need for further assessment and modification of the care plan. The midwife should identify possible causes, provide appropriate additional support and reassess the effectiveness of revised interventions.

questions.question_text: A midwife plans to reduce a pregnant woman's risk of dehydration through oral fluid intake, provided there is no clinical contraindication. Which finding would best indicate improvement?

choices.text: The woman reports improved thirst and has adequate urine output with stable clinical observations
The woman refuses all oral fluids
The woman's urine output decreases further
The woman develops increasing dizziness and dry mucous membranes

questions.rationale: Improved hydration may be reflected in reduced thirst, adequate urine output and stable clinical findings. The midwife should interpret these findings alongside the woman's overall condition and any relevant fluid balance assessment.

questions.question_text: A midwife records a woman's blood pressure as 170/115 mmHg but does not document any action taken. What is the most important improvement to the record?

choices.text: Remove the blood pressure reading from the record
Document the assessment, clinical response, interventions, escalation and subsequent findings with times
Record only the name of the midwife on duty
Wait until the end of the month to complete the documentation

questions.rationale: A complete clinical record should show the abnormal finding and the actions taken in response. Timely documentation supports continuity of care, clinical accountability and communication among healthcare professionals.

questions.question_text: A midwife notices that she has entered an incorrect observation in a paper-based maternity record. What is the correct action?

choices.text: Erase the incorrect entry completely so that no trace remains
Use correction fluid to cover the incorrect information
Correct the entry according to facility policy, preserving the original information and adding the required date, time and authentication
Ask another midwife to rewrite the entire record without explanation

questions.rationale: Clinical records must remain accurate, transparent and traceable. Corrections should follow facility policy and must not conceal or destroy the original entry.

questions.question_text: A midwife is using the SOAP format to document a woman's complaint of severe headache during pregnancy. Which entry belongs in the Subjective section?

choices.text: Blood pressure measured at 165/110 mmHg
The woman states, 'I have had a severe headache since this morning'
The midwife assesses the woman as having suspected severe pre-eclampsia
Urgent referral is arranged

questions.rationale: The subjective section contains information reported by the woman, including symptoms and personal experiences. Measured blood pressure is objective data, while clinical interpretation and planned actions belong in the assessment and plan sections.

questions.question_text: During labour monitoring, a midwife identifies an abnormal finding on the labour monitoring chart. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Record the finding accurately and take appropriate clinical action without waiting for the next routine review
Change the recorded value to make the chart appear normal
Ignore the finding if the woman is not complaining of pain
Complete the chart only after the woman has delivered

questions.rationale: Labour monitoring records are intended to support timely recognition and management of maternal or fetal abnormalities. Accurate documentation must be accompanied by appropriate assessment, escalation and intervention.

questions.question_text: A midwife is handing over a woman with suspected postpartum haemorrhage to the receiving clinical team. Which information is most important to communicate?

choices.text: Only the woman's name and date of admission
The woman's condition, estimated blood loss, vital signs, interventions performed and response to treatment
The names of all visitors who came to the ward
The midwife's personal opinion about the woman's behaviour

questions.rationale: Effective handover requires relevant, accurate and concise clinical information. Communicating the woman's condition, observations, interventions and response supports continuity and safe ongoing management.

questions.question_text: A woman in labour has a temperature of 38.5°C, maternal tachycardia and uterine tenderness. What should the midwife do FIRST?

choices.text: Assume the findings are normal during labour
Assess for possible maternal infection, including intra-amniotic infection, and promptly escalate for appropriate management
Wait until the woman develops vaginal bleeding
Discontinue maternal observations for the remainder of labour

questions.rationale: Fever, tachycardia and uterine tenderness may indicate maternal infection and require prompt clinical assessment. Early recognition and escalation support timely investigation, treatment and monitoring of maternal and fetal wellbeing.

questions.question_text: A midwife receives conflicting information about a pregnant woman's medication history. What is the most appropriate clinical reasoning approach?

choices.text: Choose one account without further investigation
Clarify the history with the woman, review available records and verify relevant information before making decisions
Ignore the medication history because the woman is pregnant
Assume that all medications previously prescribed are safe in pregnancy

questions.rationale: Clinical reasoning requires verification of relevant information before decisions are made. Clarifying the history and reviewing available records help reduce medication-related risks and support safe individualized care.

questions.question_text: A woman at 34 weeks of gestation presents with vaginal bleeding, severe abdominal pain and a rigid uterus. Her fetal heart rate is difficult to detect. Which problem should receive the highest priority?

choices.text: Anxiety related to hospital admission
Potential maternal and fetal compromise associated with suspected placental abruption
Knowledge deficit about newborn bathing
Disturbed sleep pattern related to discomfort

questions.rationale: The findings suggest possible placental abruption, which can cause severe maternal haemorrhage and fetal compromise. Immediate emergency assessment and obstetric intervention take priority over psychosocial and educational needs.

questions.question_text: A woman in labour has the following findings: respiratory rate 30 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 88%, severe breathlessness and difficulty speaking. She also reports anxiety about delivery. Which nursing problem should be prioritized?

choices.text: Anxiety related to the expected birth
Impaired gas exchange
Deficient knowledge about breastfeeding
Disturbed sleep pattern

questions.rationale: Low oxygen saturation, tachypnoea and severe breathlessness indicate impaired oxygenation and an immediate threat to life. According to physiological prioritization, respiratory compromise must be addressed before anxiety or educational needs.

questions.question_text: A postpartum woman has a temperature of 39°C, foul-smelling lochia, lower abdominal pain and a pulse rate of 120 beats per minute. Which nursing diagnosis is the most appropriate priority?

choices.text: Risk for impaired parenting
Suspected maternal infection with risk of progression to sepsis
Readiness for enhanced breastfeeding
Disturbed body image

questions.rationale: The combination of fever, foul-smelling lochia, abdominal pain and tachycardia suggests postpartum infection with possible systemic involvement. The midwife should urgently assess for sepsis and initiate escalation and management according to protocol.

questions.question_text: A midwife develops a care plan for a woman with persistent vomiting and signs of dehydration. Which expected outcome provides the best basis for evaluating the plan?

choices.text: The woman will be discharged as soon as possible
The woman will demonstrate improved hydration through appropriate clinical observations and adequate urine output within the agreed period
The woman will never experience nausea again
The midwife will administer every available antiemetic medication

questions.rationale: An effective outcome should describe a measurable improvement in the woman's condition. Clinical observations, hydration status and urine output provide relevant indicators for evaluating the response to treatment.

questions.question_text: A woman with pre-eclampsia has a care plan that includes blood pressure monitoring, assessment for warning signs and fetal surveillance. Her condition worsens despite these interventions. What is the best planning decision?

choices.text: Continue the same plan without informing the obstetric team
Reassess the woman, revise the plan and urgently escalate for further obstetric management
Remove all monitoring interventions because they have not prevented deterioration
Wait until the next routine antenatal appointment

questions.rationale: Deterioration indicates that the current care plan may no longer be sufficient to manage the woman's clinical risk. Reassessment and urgent escalation are necessary because severe pre-eclampsia may require additional treatment and timely delivery planning.

questions.question_text: A woman in labour suddenly develops convulsions and becomes unresponsive. Which action should the midwife prioritize?

choices.text: Attempt to restrain her limbs and place an object in her mouth
Call for emergency assistance, protect her from injury, maintain the airway and manage suspected eclampsia according to protocol
Leave her unattended to obtain her antenatal card
Offer oral fluids immediately

questions.rationale: Convulsions in a pregnant woman with possible hypertensive disease may indicate eclampsia, a life-threatening emergency. The midwife should protect the woman, support airway and breathing, summon help and initiate emergency management within professional competence and facility protocol.

questions.question_text: A newborn delivered at a health facility is not breathing after drying and stimulation. What should the midwife do next?

choices.text: Wait several minutes to see whether breathing starts spontaneously
Initiate neonatal resuscitation according to the current newborn resuscitation protocol, including effective ventilation when indicated
Begin routine breastfeeding immediately
Bathe the newborn to stimulate breathing

questions.rationale: A newborn who remains apnoeic or gasping after initial steps requires prompt resuscitation. Effective ventilation is the key intervention for a newborn who is not breathing adequately, and delays can worsen outcomes.

questions.question_text: A woman with postpartum haemorrhage receives treatment, and her bleeding reduces. However, she remains pale, confused and hypotensive. How should the midwife interpret these findings?

choices.text: The expected outcome has been fully achieved because visible bleeding has reduced
The woman may remain in shock despite reduced visible bleeding and requires urgent reassessment and continued emergency management
The woman should be encouraged to walk to improve circulation
Further observations are unnecessary once bleeding reduces

questions.rationale: Reduced visible bleeding does not necessarily mean that circulatory stability has been restored. Persistent hypotension, pallor and confusion suggest ongoing or unresolved shock and require immediate reassessment and continued treatment.

questions.question_text: A newborn receiving care for suspected infection has worsening respiratory distress, poor feeding and reduced responsiveness. The original care plan focused mainly on maintaining warmth and feeding support. What is the most appropriate evaluation decision?

choices.text: Continue the original plan because it was already documented
Determine that the newborn's condition is deteriorating and urgently escalate for assessment and treatment of possible serious neonatal illness
Discontinue observations to allow the newborn to rest
Record that the newborn is improving because feeding support was provided

questions.rationale: Worsening respiratory distress, poor feeding and reduced responsiveness are danger signs requiring urgent clinical intervention. Evaluation must identify deterioration and lead to immediate modification of care and escalation.

questions.question_text: A midwife documents that a woman has a blood pressure of 168/112 mmHg but records that she is stable and requires no further action. The woman also has severe headache and visual disturbance. What is the main problem with this documentation?

choices.text: The blood pressure should not be recorded in a maternity record
The clinical interpretation and documented plan do not appropriately reflect the danger signs and need for urgent escalation
The midwife should record only the woman's subjective complaints
The documentation is acceptable because the woman is still conscious

questions.rationale: Severe hypertension accompanied by headache and visual disturbance is concerning for pre-eclampsia with severe features. Documentation must accurately reflect the clinical risk and the urgent assessment, intervention and escalation required.

questions.question_text: A woman is referred from a CHPS compound to a district hospital because of suspected obstructed labour. The referral note contains only her name and gestational age. Which information is most important to add?

choices.text: The midwife's personal comments about the woman's family
Relevant clinical findings, labour history, maternal and fetal observations, interventions, time of referral and reason for escalation
A list of unrelated patients seen at the CHPS compound
Only the woman's preferred newborn name

questions.rationale: A referral note should provide sufficient clinical information for the receiving team to continue care safely. Relevant findings, interventions and the reason for referral help prevent delays and support continuity of emergency obstetric management.

questions.question_text: A woman in the third trimester reports reduced fetal movement. The fetal heart rate is initially detected at 140 beats per minute, but the woman continues to report that movement is significantly reduced. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

choices.text: The normal fetal heart rate completely excludes fetal compromise
The woman's concern still requires appropriate assessment because a single normal fetal heart rate does not establish overall fetal wellbeing
The midwife should dismiss the report because the fetal heart rate is within the usual range
The woman should be advised to return only if she develops contractions

questions.rationale: A fetal heart rate within the expected range at one point does not rule out all causes of reduced fetal movement or guarantee continuing fetal wellbeing. The midwife should arrange appropriate further assessment and follow the relevant referral or monitoring pathway.

questions.question_text: A midwife is caring for a woman in labour whose partograph shows slow cervical dilatation, but maternal observations and fetal heart rate remain reassuring. A colleague recommends immediate caesarean birth based only on the cervical dilatation rate. What is the best response?

choices.text: Proceed immediately because slow cervical dilatation always requires caesarean birth
Review the complete clinical picture, labour progress, maternal and fetal condition, and current labour management guidance before deciding on intervention
Ignore the labour monitoring chart because maternal and fetal observations are reassuring
Discontinue monitoring until cervical dilatation improves

questions.rationale: A single measure of cervical dilatation should not be used in isolation to determine the need for operative birth. Clinical decisions should consider the overall labour pattern, maternal and fetal wellbeing, and current evidence-based guidance.

questions.question_text: A midwife at a resource-limited maternity facility identifies a woman with severe vaginal bleeding. The facility has limited blood supplies and no operating theatre. Which decision best demonstrates sound clinical reasoning?

choices.text: Continue routine observation until the available blood supply is replenished
Recognize the emergency, initiate available stabilization measures, summon assistance and coordinate urgent transfer to a facility with appropriate resources
Discharge the woman because the facility lacks an operating theatre
Delay referral until all routine documentation has been completed

questions.rationale: The midwife must recognize the limits of the facility while taking immediate steps to reduce risk and secure definitive care. Appropriate stabilization, communication and urgent referral are essential in resource-limited settings.
